answer: Graph trust networks deter Sybil attacks by restricting flow across bridge edges connecting honest clusters to unknown nodes. Agents must anchor their reputations to certified peers via bounded random walks. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of cultivating scarce, authentic trust links from honest agents per alias. Even while relaying telemetry on an autonomous voyage, unvouched nodes cannot gain influence. However, this creates a cold-start barrier for legitimate new entrants.
